security_spec.violation_condition: In XiangShan RTL, the FPU conversion pipeline incorrectly applies the integer-range validity check from the int_conv table (designed for FCVT.W[U].S and FCVT.L[U].S) to the FCVT.D.S (double-to-single) instruction. Specifically, the fcvtds decoder maps to the same validity-checking micro-op or the FCVT.D.S execution unit shares a common valid-input-range comparator with the integer-conversion FCVT instructions, causing a double-precision floating-point operand to be compared against the 32-bit or 64-bit signed/unsigned integer representable range. When the double-precision value lies outside the integer range (e.g., 1e100, NaN, infinity), the hardware incorrectly asserts the NV (Invalid Operation) flag in fflags and writes the clipped integer-bound value instead of the correctly rounded single-precision result.
security_spec.summary: FCVT.D.S must NOT share the integer-range validity check with FCVT.W[U]/L[U].S; misapplying the int_conv table to double-to-single conversion causes spurious NV exceptions and corrupted conversion results

findings.finding: isFpWidenNext (FCVT.D.S lands here) and isFp2IntNext are derived from mutually exclusive conditions: outIsFpNext && isWiden vs. !outIsFpNext. FCVT.D.S uses vfwcvt_ffv='b11_001100' (bit6=1 → outIsFpNext=true, bit4=0,bit3=1 → isWiden=true). Integer FCVTs (e.g., vfcvt_xufv='b10_000000') have bit6=0 → outIsFpNext=false → isFp2IntNext=true. The two paths are structurally exclusive.
findings.snippet:
val (isFpWidenNext, isFpNarrowNext, isFp2IntNext, isFpCrossHighNext, isFpCrossLowNext) =
  (outIsFpNext && isWiden, outIsFpNext && isNarrow, !outIsFpNext,
    outIsFpNext && isCrossHigh, outIsFpNext && isCrossLow)

findings.finding: The fp→fp widen branch (where FCVT.D.S executes) sets NV only for SNaN canonicalization (isSNaNSrc && !s1_fpCanonicalNAN). of, uf, nx are hardwired to false.B. There is no integer-range check (ofExpRounded, toUnv, toInv) in this branch. The rounded result is correctly built from sign/exp/frac via fpWidenResultMapGen — a proper IEEE 754 widen operation.

when(isFpWiden || isFpCrossHigh){

findings.finding: The .otherwise branch (fp→int) at line 617 is syntactically unreachable when isFpWiden=true. Chisel when/elsewhen/otherwise compiles to a priority MUX tree; the nv/integer-overflow logic (ofExpRounded, toUnv, toInv at lines 625-653) is physically gated off for fp→fp conversions. The verified hardware does NOT share a comparator between FCVT.D.S and integer FCVT instructions.

In the scalar FPU FPToInt module, fp→fp conversions are handled entirely within the 'when (in.bits.wflags && !in.bits.ren2)' block (line 601). Widening (FCVT.D.S, outTag>inTag) only canonicalizes NaN at line 604. Narrowing (FCVT.S.D, outTag<inTag) delegates to hardfloat.RecFNToRecFN at line 612. Neither path touches the RecFNToIN (fp→int) module at line 491, which is in a completely separate class (FPToInt vs. IntToFP).

vfwcvt_ffv encoding 'b11_001100' is correct. Bit[6]=1 (output is fp), bits[5:4]=00, bits[3:2]=11 (widen), bits[1:0]=00. The hardware dispatch at CVT64.scala:183 reads bit[6] as outIsFpNext, and bits[4:3] as isWiden/isNarrow. This matches the encoding table exactly.

Scalar FPU decoder maps FCVT_D_S to typeTagIn=S, typeTagOut=D with cvt=Y, wflags=Y. This correctly dispatches to IntToFP (IntToFP.scala:601), the fp-to-fp conversion pipe. The RecFNToIN (fp→int) path at FPToInt.scala:491 is in a separate Chisel module class and cannot be reached by FCVT.D.S.
